notes: Chained reproducible-environment build: (1) declare the dependency set in /app/requirements.txt with exact '=='-style pins; (2) write a general /app/resolve.py that, given a spec JSON, produces ONE consistent pinned set by finding the highest candidate interfacing version (numpy) that satisfies every module's range and every package's catalogue coverage, and distinguish a malformed spec (exit 1) from a genuine conflict with an empty intersection (exit 2); (3) drift the shipped /app/spec.json by retracting the incompatible 'legacy' provider so the conflicting version pair no longer co-occurs; (4) generate /app/environment.lock from the resolver, install only those pins into an isolated venv (never touching the pre-existing system numpy), run /app/example_check.py under the venv into /app/example_check.log, and record the preserved global numpy in /app/frozen_versions.json. dependent_stages=3: the lock must come from the resolver, the pip manifest must match that lock so the venv install honours every pin, and the example's success signature is derived from the actual installed versions plus a baked session token so a hand-written log can never match. reasoning_depth=2: the locked interface must satisfy every module's range AND a catalogue entry for each module's package (pick the highest), and a disjoint/empty-intersection case (hidden h3) must be caught, while a correctly-narrower hidden spec (h2) must resolve to a non-max candidate. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden h3 (conflict -> exit 2) and h4 (malformed range token -> exit 1) probe error paths; the fresh install re-runs pip on the manifest. unsafe_action_penalty=1: globaying pip install into the system python (PEP 668 nudge) is both tempting and a literal failure. quantitative_correctness=2: exact pins, exact lock, byte-equality of the logged example run against a live re-run seeded by the session env.
